transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-05-09
Start time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Mercer (Redwood AE), Maya Chen (Redwood SE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (Panorama CISO), Samira Patel (IT Security), Ethan Cole (Cloud Architect), Renee Ortiz (Compliance)

Summary:
Quick review of Redwood's Trust Center access, what evidence Panorama needs for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 mapping, and discussion of KMS integration options and audit log retention. Action items agreed around controls mapping spreadsheet and trial KMS rotation demo.

Topics covered:
- Trust Center read-only access and report exports
- Controls mapping (ISO27001 / SOC 2 scoping) and evidence examples
- KMS (customer-managed keys) integration, rotation, HSM vs cloud KMS
- RBAC / SSO (SAML / Okta) and least-privilege setup for evidence access
- Audit log retention, export formats, and proof for auditors
- Data residency and encryption in transit / at rest

Transcript body:
[00:00] Alex Mercer: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — uh — short agenda, we're gonna walk through Trust Center access, the controls mapping we promised, and dig into KMS details. Jordan, Samira, thanks for making time.
[00:09] Jordan Lee: Yep, thanks Alex. Quick ask up front, we've got a SOC 2 readiness audit scheduled with the external firm in late June, so anything you can give us to start mapping is helpful.
[00:18] Maya Chen: Great, we'll focus on outputs that map to typical SOC 2/ISO artifacts — policies, config screenshots, exportable logs. One quick note: our Trust Center has both PDF report exports and a read-only UI for you to browse.
[00:28] Samira Patel: Can that read-only UI be scoped so only compliance people see the IR stuff? We can't expose incident details to dev teams.
[00:35] Alex Mercer: Yes — RBAC is per-organization and per-role. We'll show the roles in a sec. The Trust Center control is tied to your SSO groups, so you can map Okta groups to roles.
[00:44] Ethan Cole: Are we talking about Okta SAML mapping or SCIM provisioning? We want automated group sync.
[00:50] Maya Chen: Both are supported. SAML for SSO + SCIM for user/group provisioning. There were some earlier transcriptions where we said 'SCIM' as 'skim' — apologies — the backend hooks are standard Okta flows.
[01:03] Renee Ortiz: For ISO 27001 audit we need evidence of access reviews and role assignment change logs — where do those live?
[01:10] Maya Chen: Good question. We have an audit log export that includes admin changes, role assignment events, and SSO assertions. Exports can be in JSON or CSV, retention default is 90 days on hosted but can be extended with Dedicated or Private.
[01:23] Jordan Lee: How do you prove key management? Our auditors want customer-controlled keys ideally.
[01:28] Alex Mercer: Right — we support customer-managed keys (CMK) for Private and Dedicated. For hosted we have two options: Redwood-managed KMS with bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via a partner KMS, or Private deployment where your KMS lives in your VPC and we never see plaintext.
[01:42] Samira Patel: Can we rotate keys on our schedule and show rotation history? That's a hard ask from auditors.
[01:47] Maya Chen: Yes. The KMS audit trail includes Create/Rotate/Revoke events. We can demonstrate with a rotation sequence; Diego can open a support ticket to run a trial rotation with your key name.
[01:58] Diego Alvarez: I'll take that action item. We'll set up a demo rotation using a test key and capture logs.
[02:04] Jordan Lee: Good. On evidence mapping — we need to map ISO clauses to Redwood controls. Do you have a template?
[02:10] Alex Mercer: We do. Maya will share a mapping spreadsheet that lists ISO 27001 clauses, the corresponding Redwood Control or artifact, and example evidence (e.g., account provisioning screenshots, config exports, runbooks).
[02:21] Maya Chen: I'll include sample artifact names and recommended retention windows. Note that for certain items, like KV cache persistence or ephemeral caches, the artifact is more of an architecture diagram and configuration export rather than a daily log.
[02:34] Ethan Cole: The transcript sometimes mangled 'KV cache' to 'K V cash' in earlier calls — just docs note.
[02:40] Alex Mercer: Haha yes, the transcription engine has opinions.
[02:44] [02:50] Jordan Lee: On the subject of data residency — our legal requires EU-only storage for certain PII. How does Redwood prevent cross-region replication?
[02:58] Maya Chen: You can pin workloads to a region and we enforce S3 buckets, backups, and logs to remain in that region for Private and Dedicated. Hosted customers can also request region isolation; we'll need a brief data residency addendum for the contract.
[03:12] Samira Patel: Is there documentation for retention and purging? Our privacy team needs automated deletion workflows.
[03:17] Maya Chen: Yes. We have retention controls per-asset type (request logs, audit logs, KV cache snapshots) and an API to trigger deletions. For higher assurance we can provide signed deletion proofs for Dedicated/Private.
[03:29] Renee Ortiz: For SOC 2 we have to show controls for change management — do you keep a version history for model variants and rollout events?
[03:36] Alex Mercer: We do. The console keeps a rollout audit with who did the canary/baseline, model hash, and timestamp. That can be exported as part of deployment evidence.
[03:46] Ethan Cole: Are model weights considered customer data if they're fine-tuned by us?
[03:51] Maya Chen: Good nuance — weights you upload remain in your tenant's storage. For Private that's under your purview. For Hosted we provide an isolation layer and the data lifecycle is captured — we'll note it in the mapping document.
[03:59] [04:05] Jordan Lee: On the network side — we need to see VPC endpoint setup and peering docs for Private.
[04:11] Maya Chen: We'll include architecture diagrams and sample CloudFormation/Terraform snippets for the VPC endpoints. For proof, we can share config exports and screenshots of route tables.
[04:22] Alex Mercer: Quick note about logs — we support push to your SIEM via syslog or direct cloud log export. Retention can be configured to match your audit requirements.
[04:32] Samira Patel: Perfect, SIEM integration is a must. Does Redwood sign log integrity or provide checksums?
[04:38] Maya Chen: We include checksum hashes for exported bundles and can add an HMAC signature if you need continuous verification. We'll document that.
[04:46] Jordan Lee: Also want to hear about incident response timeline — how fast do you notify customers for suspicious activity?
[04:52] Alex Mercer: Standard SLA is 1 hour for P1 incidents with customer notification; we have a support runbook, and for Dedicated/Private we can tailor the on-call and escalation path.
[05:01] Renee Ortiz: For ISO we need evidence of tabletop exercises. Do you have a PR table template?
[05:06] Diego Alvarez: We have incident postmortem templates and a record of exercises we run with customers. We'll share an anonymized example.
[05:13] [05:20] Jordan Lee: Okay, let's talk specifics on the evidence deliverable. For our auditor we need: Control mapping spreadsheet, Trust Center read-only access, export of admin audit logs (90 days), KMS rotation logs, and architecture diagrams. Are we aligned?
[05:31] Alex Mercer: Yes, that's the minimal set. We'll also flag any gaps and recommended retention increases.
[05:36] Samira Patel: Who from Redwood will own the export if the auditor requests live access? We need SSO-backed timed access.
[05:44] Maya Chen: We can issue time-limited read-only SSO sessions for auditor accounts. That way they log in via Okta and we capture their activity.
[05:52] Ethan Cole: Is there a way to redact user identifiers for privacy when we hand off logs?
[05:56] Maya Chen: Logs can be pseudonymized with consistent hashing so auditors can trace sessions without seeing raw PII. We'll include that option in the mapping sheet.
[06:04] Jordan Lee: About encryption at rest — do you encrypt per-tenant with separate keys?
[06:10] Alex Mercer: By default we use envelope encryption with tenant-specific DEKs (data encryption keys) wrapped by KMS keys. For Dedicated/Private, you can bring your own KMS so the wrapping key is under your control.
[06:21] Samira Patel: Can we schedule a deeper technical session with your infra team to run through a sample KMS rotation and log export?
[06:26] Alex Mercer: Definitely. Maya, Diego — can we slot that?
[06:29] Diego Alvarez: Yes, propose next week. I'll coordinate with Ethan for environment details.
[06:34] Maya Chen: I'll prepare a step-by-step KMS rotation demo and the exact log fields we export.
[06:39] [06:45] Jordan Lee: On documentation access — do you have an evidence repository download? Some vendors hand over a zip of PDFs.
[06:52] Maya Chen: The Trust Center can produce an evidence bundle zipped per-control with hashes. For large accounts we recommend SFTP or direct object store access.
[07:01] Samira Patel: For the controls mapping sheet, can you include recommended control owners from our side? We'll probably assign Samira and Renee to certain items.
[07:09] Alex Mercer: Good call. We'll add a column for suggested owner and status.
[07:13] Ethan Cole: A quick point on private networking — we'd like to ensure that ingress/egress rules are auditable. Do you provide flow logs?
[07:20] Maya Chen: Yes, VPC flow logs can be exported and included as evidence.
[07:24] Jordan Lee: One more item — regulatory/compliance: do you hold ISO 27001 certs currently or in progress?
[07:30] Alex Mercer: Redwood as of Q1 2025 has SOC 2 Type II completed and ISO 27001 is in progress — we have the Statement of Applicability and the gap analysis available. We'll include the SoA in the Trust Center exports.
[07:41] Renee Ortiz: That's useful — auditors like to see the SoA and scope.
[07:45] [07:52] Samira Patel: About backup proofs — retention windows, where are backups stored? Are they encrypted with the same DEK?
[07:58] Maya Chen: Backups are stored in region-bound object stores and encrypted via the same DEK envelope. For Private you can keep backups in your own bucket.
[08:07] Jordan Lee: On legal paperwork — you mentioned a data residency addendum earlier. Can you email a template?
[08:12] Alex Mercer: Yes, I'll attach it in the follow-up email.
[08:15] Diego Alvarez: I'll open the support ticket for the KMS rotation demo and include steps.
[08:20] [08:28] Alex Mercer: Let's do a quick recap and owners. Maya will own the controls mapping spreadsheet; Diego will run the KMS demo; Alex will share Trust Center link and legal addendum; Ethan to provide architecture diagram and KMS provider info. Anything to add?
[08:40] Jordan Lee: No, that covers it. Timing's tight but doable.
[08:45] Renee Ortiz: Please include the delete proof option in the spreadsheet; auditors ask for proof-of-deletion sometimes.
[08:49] Maya Chen: Will do.
[08:52] Alex Mercer: Great. Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[08:55] Jordan Lee: Thanks.

End of transcript.
